newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway says U.N.-Iraq oil deal should go ahead.
newsitem.headline: Norway says U.N.-Iraq oil deal should go ahead.

text.p: Norway said on Thursday the United Nations oil-for-food deal with Iraq should go ahead without delay despite the latest military skirmishes between Baghdad and the U.S.

Deputy Foreign Minister Jan Egeland said Norway supported punitive measures against Iraqi President Saddam Hussein, but not the prolonged suffering of Iraqi civilians, already hard hit by more than six years of U.N. sanctions.
A trade embargo was imposed against Iraq in August 1990 after its troops invaded Kuwait.
"This scheme was intended to help innocent Iraqi civilians who have been hurt by the international sanctions," Egeland told Reuters.
"Saddam's new aggression is an argument for a prolongation of the sanctions but should not delay the oil-for-food agreement. That should be seen totally separately from the acts of the dictator."
The deal allows Baghdad to sell up to $2 billion of oil over six months to pay for badly needed food and medicines.
The plan was suspended on September 1 by U.N. Secretary General Boutros Boutros-Ghali after Iraq sent troops into a Kurdish area in the north of the country to help a Kurdish leader rout a rival.
Norway, which is part of an international group selected to oversee the oil sales, supported the U.S. punitive action against the Iraqi stance.
